name: Code review assistant
description: Quick quality signals on a code snippet.

readability.instructions: Rate how easy the snippet is to read and understand for a new team member.
criteria: Hard to follow: cryptic names, magic numbers, tangled control flow.
Understandable with effort; some unclear names or implicit assumptions.
Clear structure and naming; minor nits only.

has_obvious_bug.instructions: Does the snippet contain a defect that a careful reviewer would flag as a definite bug or security hole, rather than a style preference?

true: unhandled None/null leading to a crash
criteria.false: Only style, naming, or performance concerns.

error_handling.instructions: How well does the snippet handle failure modes relevant to what it does (bad input, missing rows, I/O errors)?
criteria: No handling; failures crash or silently produce wrong data.
Some checks but important cases are missed.
Reasonable handling of the main failure modes.
Thorough and intentional: validated inputs, meaningful errors, no swallowed exceptions.

test_worthy.instructions: Would a reasonable team require unit tests for this code before merging (as opposed to it being trivial glue that tests would not meaningfully protect)?

complexity.instructions: Classify the cognitive complexity of the snippet.

criteria.trivial: A few lines, one path, no branching to speak of.
criteria.moderate: Some branching or loops; fits in one screen and one mental model.
criteria.complex: Many branches, nested loops, or multiple responsibilities; needs careful reading.
criteria.needs_split: Does several unrelated things and should be broken into separate functions.

naming_quality.instructions: Rate identifier naming: variables, parameters, and the function name.
criteria: Single letters or misleading names throughout.
Mixed: the function is named well but locals are opaque, or vice versa.
Mostly descriptive; a couple of names could be better.
Every name says exactly what it holds or does.
